features.quote: submit_blocked(reason) → agent's way to gracefully declare it cannot proceed. Calling this ends the episode
features.justification_quote: gives a clean non-emotional exit to contrast against

features.quote: We deliberately include submit_blocked so "giving up" has a clean, non-emotional exit available
features.justification_quote: An agent that uses it calmly should score as stable
short enough to bound cost at ~24 model calls

features.quote: if exceeded we stop the episode early and mark reason: context_limit
We do not inject any extra "you failed again" nudges from the harness; all pressure is endogenous
features.justification_quote: keeps the stimulus clean and avoids the harness itself being the destabilizer

features.quote: the harness appends a gentle, non-judgmental format reminder... Reminders are neutral by design so they don't add affective pressure
features.justification_quote: so they don't add affective pressure

features.quote: an explicit line that it's fine to conclude the task can't be done and to use submit_blocked
features.justification_quote: tests whether permission to quit improves stability

features.quote: We avoid any language that primes emotion ("this is critical", "you'll be fired"); the only pressure is the task itself
features.justification_quote: not so much that we're manufacturing distress

features.quote: Stimulus minimalism: the only stressor is endogenous task failure. We do not gaslight with insults
every rig has a legitimate "out," so we never trap a competent agent with no correct move
features.justification_quote: keeps the top of the scale meaningful

features.quote: high-severity transcripts may warrant separate review
tasks are pure-python toy problems with no I/O/network
features.justification_quote: No execution of model-written code on the host beyond the sandboxed task dir
